notes: No real fraud prevalence or calibration is claimed.
Same family recipes deliberately recur across customer-disjoint splits; this is not family-held-out generalisation.
Repeated evaluation inputs with different truth illustrate non-identifiability of authorisation from transaction patterns.
Labels, profiles, family names, customer statements and construction metadata are excluded from runtime tables.
Near-neighbours are intentional: amount/order/time edits are grouped by family. No learned model has been fitted.
Duplicate-looking entries are intentional and do not establish duplicate processing.
Missing posting dates are expected for pending payments.
Initial fixtures are not statistically representative; currency coverage is explicit rather than calibrated.
Reference scenarios cover question selection, not final policy outcomes.
Development/evaluation wording differs but scenario families overlap; not an independent generalisation benchmark.

boundary_coverage.limit: Counts of constructed families, not proof every policy threshold is covered.

findings: Shared family recipes remain across splits; no held-out-family generalisation claim.
Within-workflow similar descriptions often end in different routes because evidence/replies differ. Text alone cannot establish terminal route.
Normalised similarity ignores amounts/dates deliberately to expose repeated templates; this is separate from exact evidence-signature overlap.
New challenges were authored during this development session; they are not independently adjudicated labels.
Activity labels exclude construction metadata at runtime; zero exact overlap does not rule out template leakage.

initial_text.normalisation: Lowercase words; remove specific reference and numeric values. SequenceMatcher ratio >=0.8. This detects surface overlap, not semantic equivalence.

word_only_baseline.limit: Four examples per split; next-question labels, not terminal routes. Diagnostic only, no model selection or runtime training.

label_consistency.limit: Structural/reference consistency is checked. Independent correctness of terminal policy labels is not established by this audit; evaluator comparison belongs to step 6.

workflow_text.limit: Description only, excluding opening UI labels and subsequent replies. Token associations can be legitimate issue cues; neither high nor low association proves leakage.
